title: Berlin registry of transcatheter mitral valve interventions (BTMVI)
summary:
Catheter-based heart valve interventions were initially used in inoperable patients with very high surgical risk. In recent years, the indications for transcatheter valve interventions have expanded considerably. Despite growing clinical experience and increasing use, scientific data on transcatheter mitral valve interventions remain limited. In particular, evidence regarding post-interventional management and the factors influencing outcomes after mitral valve interventions is scarce. To date, transcatheter mitral valve interventions are performed only in specialized centers.

The aim of the registry is to generate new insights based on data from routine clinical practice in order to improve outcomes after transcatheter mitral valve interventions. Another objective is to identify relevant predictors of increased procedural risk, thereby enabling therapeutic decision-making to be based on a stronger scientific foundation. Both currently available mitral valve interventions and all future types of mitral valve procedures used in routine clinical practice at the Deutsches Herzzentrum der Charité will be prospectively included in this registry.
